trim_surface_input_group.description: Rate per LF applies to aggregate trim LF across all in-scope items. Engine sums LF from all active trim items and divides by rate to calculate hours.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Setup (Perimeter Drops)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Runner-style drop cloths along trim perimeter. ~12 sec per SF. Same rate as paint counterpart.

task_production_rates.name: Wall Masking at Trim Edge
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tape + paper masking at trim-to-wall edge. ~24 sec per LF. Same rate as paint counterpart.

task_production_rates.name: Cover Fixtures Near Spray Zone
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tape over outlet/switch plates. ~2 min per fixture.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Bare Wood

QT3.notes: Quick scan — obvious defects, mill marks, open nail holes

QT4.notes: Systematic inspection — mark all visible defects, check grain

QT5.notes: Thorough inspection under raking light — every imperfection

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Visual inspection of bare wood trim. Same tiered rates as paint counterpart inspection tasks.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Bare Wood (120 Grit)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Initial bare wood sanding with 120-grit. ~36 sec per LF. Stock removal of mill marks. Slower than prep sanding on primed surface.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Bare Wood (150 Grit)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final prep sand with 150-grit. ~30 sec per LF. Finer grit = faster pass (less stock removal).

task_production_rates.name: Fill Defects (Stainable Wood Filler)

QT3.notes: Fill open nail holes and obvious dents

QT5.notes: Fill every defect — color-match filler to stain

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walk rate including inspection and fill. QT5 slower due to color-matching filler and filling smallest defects.

task_production_rates.name: Grain Raise Treatment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Wet wipe + dry time + re-sand 220. ~24 sec per LF for wipe + sand (dry time is wait, not labor). Conditional on waterborne products.

task_production_rates.name: Tack Clean (Prep Complete)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth wipe all trim surfaces. ~6 sec per LF. Same pace at all tiers.

task_production_rates.name: Apply Wood Conditioner
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush on conditioner liberally. ~18 sec per LF. Fast application — no precision needed.

task_production_rates.name: Wipe Excess Conditioner
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Wipe off excess conditioner. ~12 sec per LF. Quick pass.

task_production_rates.name: Stain Coat 1 — Brush + Wipe
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush stain + wipe. ~45 sec per LF. Includes dwell + wipe time. Brush gives most control over color uniformity.

task_production_rates.name: Stain Coat 1 — Roll + Wipe
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roll stain with foam roller + wipe. ~30 sec per LF. Faster application than brush. Foam roller avoids lint.

task_production_rates.name: Stain Coat 1 — Spray + Wipe
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray stain + wipe. ~36 sec per LF. Fast spray offset by wipe step. Back-brush into profiles recommended.

task_production_rates.name: Stain Coat 2 — Apply + Wipe
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second stain coat. ~36 sec per LF. Slightly faster than coat 1 — less absorption on second pass. Rate is average across methods.

task_production_rates.name: Verify Stain Dry
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fixed time: ~10 min per session. Touch test in inconspicuous areas. Not continuous labor — spot checks.

task_production_rates.name: Apply Sanding Sealer (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Thin sealer coat. ~30 sec per LF. Fast application — sealer is thin and spreads easily. Rate for brush method. Spray: ~160 LF/hr.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Sealer (220 Grit)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Sand sealer with 220 grit. ~24 sec per LF. Sealer sands very easily (designed for sanding).

task_production_rates.name: Tack Clean Between Sealer Coats
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth wipe. ~6 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.name: Apply Sanding Sealer (Coat 2)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second sealer coat. ~28 sec per LF. Slightly faster than coat 1 — consistent substrate.

task_production_rates.name: Final Sealer Sand (320 Grit)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fine sand with 320 grit. ~20 sec per LF. Finer grit = faster pass. Creates glass-smooth base for clear.

task_production_rates.name: Tack Clean Before Clear Coat
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth wipe. ~6 sec per LF. Critical before clear coat.

task_production_rates.name: Clear Coat 1 — Brush
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush clear coat 1. ~36 sec per LF. Faster than stain (no wipe step). Strain clear before pour.

task_production_rates.name: Clear Coat 1 — Spray
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray clear coat 1. ~24 sec per LF. HVLP preferred for clear. Consistent distance and speed.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Clear Coat (320-400 Grit)

QT5.notes: Full surface sand. 400 grit (finer = faster pass).

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clear interstage sanding. QT3 spot sand only. QT4 full 320. QT5 full 400 (finer grit paradoxically faster — very light touch).

task_production_rates.name: Tack Clean Between Clear Coats
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth wipe. ~6 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Clear Coat
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Visual inspection between clear coats. Same tiered rates as paint interstage inspection.

task_production_rates.name: Clear Coat 2
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clear coat 2 brush. ~33 sec per LF. Faster than coat 1 — consistent substrate. Rate for brush; spray is ~170 LF/hr.

task_production_rates.name: Clear Coat 3
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clear coat 3. Same rate as coat 2 — consistent substrate.

task_production_rates.name: Protection Teardown
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all protection. ~7.2 sec per SF. Teardown faster than setup. Careful tape removal near fresh clear coat.

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum Sanding Dust
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fixed time: ~20 min per session. Stain/clear work generates dust from 5+ sanding stages. More dust than paint specs.

task_production_rates.name: Final Inspection

QT3.notes: Quick glance — no obvious defects, uniform color

QT4.notes: Systematic scan — uniform color and sheen

QT5.notes: Critical inspection — zero tolerance, uniform color and sheen across all surfaces

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final quality check. Same tiered rates as paint counterpart final inspection.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up

QT5.notes: Address every imperfection — may need full coat over repairs

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Touch-up defects from final inspection. Walk rate with spot work.

quality_tier_effects.description: Budget stain/clear — baseline rates, minimal coats
quality_tier_effects.notes: QT3 default: 1 stain + 0 sealer + 1 clear = 2 total coats. Spot sand between coats. Quick inspection.

quality_tier_effects.description: Standard stain/clear — full sand, systematic inspection
quality_tier_effects.notes: QT4 default: 1 stain + 1 sealer + 2 clear = 4 total coats. Full sand between coats. Professional residential standard.

quality_tier_effects.description: Premium stain/clear — maximum coats, thorough sand, zero tolerance
quality_tier_effects.notes: QT5 default: 1 stain + 2 sealer + 3 clear = 6 total coats. 400-grit between clear coats. Critical inspection.

profile_complexity_modifiers.notes: 15% time reduction. Simple profiles stain and sand faster. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 7.2.

profile_complexity_modifiers.description: Ogee, cove, or standard residential profiles

profile_complexity_modifiers.notes: 25% time increase. More edges, crevices, stain pooling in profiles. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 7.2.

profile_complexity_modifiers.description: Dentil, egg-and-dart, or highly detailed profiles
profile_complexity_modifiers.notes: 40% time increase. Maximum detail density. Stain and clear both pool in detail crevices. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 7.2.

height_access_effects.notes: Floor-level access. Baseline. Most trim types.

height_access_effects.description: Tall 9-12 ft working height (crown, picture rail)
height_access_effects.notes: Step/extension ladder. Primarily crown molding and upper trim.
Scaffold likely required. Rare for standard residential trim.

rate_notes.multi_surface_aggregation: This spec covers 7 trim types (door casing and window casing excluded), all measured in LF. Production rates apply per LF regardless of which trim type the footage comes from.
rate_notes.stain_wipe_included: All stain application rates INCLUDE the wipe step. The rate is for apply + dwell + wipe as a single operation. Wipe is not a separate task.
rate_notes.sealer_and_clear_method: Sealer and clear use the same application method (application_method_clear). Rates shown are for brush method. Spray rates are approximately 30-50% faster.
rate_notes.modifier_application: Modifiers increase TIME, not rate. effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. Modifiers stack multiplicatively: total_modifier = profile_complexity x height x QT (for qt_scaled tasks).
rate_notes.coat_count_driven: Total labor is primarily driven by coat count. QT5 default of 6 total coats is 3x the labor of QT3 default of 2 coats, before QT-scaled task adjustments.

assumptions.value: Stain application rates include dwell time + wipe. Not modeled as separate tasks.
assumptions.source: Industry practice — wipe is integral to stain application
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines stain wipe as separate vs integrated task. Integrated approach matches field practice.

assumptions.value: Clear coat 2 and coat 3 use the same rate (110 LF/hr brush). Consistent substrate after coat 1.
assumptions.note: Same assumption as paint spec coat 2/3 rates.
